title: A Two-Dimensional Counterexample to Radical Equality in Primitive Axial Algebras
summary: Let $R(A,X)$ denote the largest ideal of a primitive axial algebra $(A,X)$ that contains no axis from the specified generating set $X$, and let $J(A)$ be the intersection of the maximal ideals of $A$. Mamontov, Shpectorov, and Zhelyabin asked whether $R(A,X)=J(A)$ always holds. We give a negative answer. Over every field of characteristic different from $2$, the two-dimensional commutative algebra with basis $a,b$ and multiplication $a^2=a$, $ab=2b$, and $b^2=b$ is a primitive axial algebra for an explicit fusion law and the generating set $X={a,b}$.
